newsitem.title: DENMARK: New diabetes drugs seen hurting Novo.
newsitem.headline: New diabetes drugs seen hurting Novo.

text.p: A new generation of oral diabetes drugs such as Warner-Lambert's Rezulin could hurt earnings for Denmark's Novo Nordisk, the world's largest insulin-maker, and rival Eli Lilly, analysts say.
"The new oral diabetic treatments will have a negative effect on insulin market growth and will hit both Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly," Lehman Brothers analyst Stewart Adkins said.
But he added that the threat depended on whether the new drugs, which stimulate secretion of insulin in the pancreas, could win documented evidence of their effectiveness.
"If the new treatments work, it won't just be a short-term effect. It will bring more of the same kind of drugs on to the market," Adkins said.
Rezulin was approved by U.S. authorities last January.
Switzerland's Novartis is expected to put its oral treatment on the market in the year 2000. Novo itself is developing a similar product, NovoNorm, which it hopes to put on sale before the millenium.
Novo sells 66 percent of its insulin to type 2 diabetes patients, the target group for the oral products.
Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Vikram P.Sahu is not convinced of the threat from Rezulin, estimating its sales for the first three months of this year at $25 million.
"Even if $25 million is only a start, its not very much. At the moment there is no great threat to the insulin market, but it is a development we are watching closely," he said.

Another analyst, who asked not to be identified, saw a fall in the insulin market coming, but only in two or three years time. Diabetes patients satisfied with their present treatment will be reluctant to change, he believes. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969653
